card: This pull request replaces the O(N log N) pairwise sorting in CTxMemPool::GetSortedScoreWithTopology() with an O(N) traversal of TxGraph's internal chunk index. Sorting the entire mempool while holding CTxMemPool::cs creates lock contention for operations such as getrawmempool, P2P mempool messages, and mempool serialization. In author benchmarks with 60k transactions, non-verbose getrawmempool time dropped from 99 ms to 24 ms, significantly reducing lock hold times for indexers.
changed_since_previous: First evaluation with diff available; no changes to the PR's implementation or commits.
evidence: Author benchmark on Ryzen 5 3600 (x86): RpcMempoolTxids with 10k transactions drops from 5.10 ms to 1.07 ms, and getrawmempool false handler with 60k transactions drops from 99 ms to 24 ms (PR description).
problem: Generating the global mempool transaction order requires sorting all transactions with TxGraph::CompareMainOrder while holding CTxMemPool::cs. Callers like getrawmempool, P2P mempool message responses, and mempool dump operations hold the mempool lock longer than necessary, causing contention for other threads.

risk.why: A bug in GetMainOrder could misorder or drop transactions in getrawmempool output, P2P mempool responses, and mempool.dat persistence.

summary: Replace the O(N log N) pairwise sorting in CTxMemPool::GetSortedScoreWithTopology() with an O(N) traversal of TxGraph's chunk index via a new TxGraph::GetMainOrder() method. The previous comparator-based sort is retained as an invariant check in CTxMemPool::check(). A new benchmark, RpcMempoolTxids, measures non-verbose getrawmempool performance.
